PLAN "12-Week Cycle-Adjusted Strength Program (Phase-aligned to Menstrual Cycle)"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Progressive resistance with cycle-aware loading"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1" (4 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday training 45m "Cycle-aware full body - Week1":
        warmup:
          running 5m
        main straight_sets:
          squat 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          bench_press 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          pull_up 3x5..8 rpe 7 rest 120 seconds
        cooldown:
          chest_stretch 3m
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Wednesday training 40m "Cycle-aware medium drive - Week1":
        warmup:
          jogging 5m
        main straight_sets:
          deadlift 3x5..8 rpe 7 rest 120 seconds
          incline_press 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          dumbbell_row 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
        cooldown:
          hip_flexor_stretch 2m
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Friday training 40m "Cycle-aware light - Week1":
        warmup:
          walking 5m
        main straight_sets:
          goblet_squat 3x12..15 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          overhead_press 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          lat_pulldown 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
        cooldown:
          shoulder_stretch 2m
    WEEK 2:
      DAY Monday training 45m "Cycle-aware progression - Week2":

          running 5m
        main straight_sets:

Notes for cycle-based adjustment:
- Flow days (cycle day 1-3) are treated as lower-intensity windows with reduced loading and avoidance of high Valsalva maneuvers, jumping, and heavy big lifts. In Phase 1 Weeks 1-2-3 and Phase 2 Week 8-11, select exercises and loads are tuned via lower reps, fewer sets, and longer rest. If symptoms intensify, replace a high-load movement with a controlled tempo or substitute a less demanding drill (e.g., switch heavy squats to goblet squats or substitute barbell work with dumbbell equivalents) during flow days.
- Outside flow days, follow standard progression with emphasis on progressive overload while respecting symptoms.
- Reassess monthly; adjust RPE targets if necessary to maintain safety and tolerability.
